skills.trigger: When evaluating a patient with dyspnea and imaging showing a right-sided pleural effusion to distinguish between common causes like heart failure and rare congenital anomalies like Scimitar syndrome.
steps: Inspect the right lower lung zone and mediastinum on axial CT or chest X-ray for a curvilinear vascular structure descending towards the right hemidiaphragm (scimitar sign).

Trace the course of this vessel to determine if it drains into the inferior vena cava (indicating Scimitar syndrome/partial anomalous pulmonary venous return) versus standard pulmonary venous drainage.

Differentiate from congestive heart failure by assessing cardiac size and looking for bilateral effusions; Scimitar syndrome typically presents with a specific unilateral vascular anomaly rather than generalized cardiomegaly and fluid overload.
